payload.task: melting_point of n-eicosane with MACE-MPA-0 (request 2ca81387-498b-4255-a877-bb17682c67ee need #0)
payload.reason: Premise check failed: the melting point of n-eicosane is well defined experimentally, but it cannot be measured credibly with MACE-MPA-0 on this hardware and budget. (1) Model domain: MACE-MPA-0 was trained on inorganic PBE/PBE+U data (MPtrj + sAlex) with no dispersion term, while alkane crystal cohesion and melting come almost entirely from interchain van der Waals forces. Test run (scripts/premise.py, float32 on an NVIDIA GB10): two parallel all-trans C20H42 chains with MACE-MPA-0 give E_int = -133 meV per CH2 at 4.2 A and still -133 meV at 3.8 A (no repulsive wall yet), -75 meV at 5.0 A, -24 meV at 6.0 A and 0 at 8.0 A, i.e. about -61 kcal/mol (about 257 kJ/mol) per chain pair. That one pair already exceeds the whole experimental sublimation enthalpy of n-eicosane (about 10^2 kJ/mol), whereas plain PBE barely binds alkanes. The interchain interaction is unphysical in both size and shape, so any Tm from it is an artefact of the model, not a prediction. The D3-corrected variant cannot be used either: torch-dftd is not installed, and it would be a different model from the one requested. (2) Size and timescale: a direct-heating Tm superheats strongly, so a credible value needs solid-liquid coexistence or free-energy methods with about 5-10k atoms (chains of about 2.5 nm), a 0.5 fs timestep (C-H) and several ns per temperature, about 10^7 steps per temperature at several temperatures. Measured throughput with the ASE MACE calculator was about 20 s per force call for 2976 atoms, so this is many orders of magnitude beyond budget even if a batched GPU pipeline were 100x faster. (3) Validation: the required independent check (the same protocol recovering n-hexadecane 291.0 +/- 1.0 K or n-octadecane 301.0 +/- 0.7 K from /data/calibration/tier1.json) has the same model-domain and cost problems, so no result could be validated. No number is reported; a value from this setup would have unknown, probably very large, error with no meaningful uncertainty. Well-posed alternatives: (a) use an organic-trained MLIP with dispersion (e.g. MACE-OFF or a model fine-tuned on dispersion-corrected molecular-crystal data), first validate it on the C16/C18 Tm and the eicosane crystal density/sublimation enthalpy, then run interface-pinning or coexistence MD on a larger GPU allocation; or (b) report the measured value 310.0 +/- 1.0 K (NIST WebBook average, tier1 calibration) as the experimental reference, not as a MACE-MPA-0 result.
